subject: APAC edge: surge of 502/504 + 429s causing client timeouts
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria@brightfield.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Brightfield Platform <brightfield-platform@brightfield.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 01:12:00 +0000
Subject: URGENT: APAC production errors — elevated 502/504 and 429s

Hi Vanessa / Marcus,

We're seeing widespread client errors from our APAC customers starting ~00:45 UTC. Scores of requests are returning 502/504 and a lot of 429 spikes. Several large clients have reported timeouts and user-facing failures (mobile and web). This is affecting the Brightfield recommendation API and is impacting paying users.

What we observed:
- 502 / 504 rate up ~7x vs baseline, concentrated on ap-northeast-1 and ap-southeast-2 front doors.
- 429s appear correlated with client retry storms (clients re-sending identical requests).
- Many requests are timing out after retries (client-side).

I attached request_logs_20260608.csv and a screenshot of the dashboard. We need a clear ETA for mitigation and whether you can route traffic to another region temporarily.

Can you confirm receipt and next steps? Our CSMs are getting escalation calls.

Thanks,
Maria Gomez
Head of Platform
Brightfield Media

Attachment: request_logs_20260608.csv (CSV, 2.1MB)
Attachment: screenshot_502_apac.png (PNG, 180KB)

From: hiro_tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai>

Cc: maria@brightfield.ai, nlb-ops@amazon.com
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 01:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: URGENT: APAC production errors — elevated 502/504 and 429s

Quick update from SRE triage (initial findings):
- Collected debug_snapshot_0608.tar.gz (attached) containing front-door metrics, per-node latencies, and sample traces.
- Observed an abrupt increase in concurrent connections at the APAC front-door NLBs starting 00:40 UTC. Backends began returning 504s as per-token generation latency rose and request queues grew.
- 429s are concentrated on a small subset of Brightfield clients that are aggressively retrying (exponential backoff not observed). These retries are amplifying backend queueing and inflight memory pressure.

Immediate mitigations we're pursuing (in parallel):
1) Apply a short-lived 50 rps token-bucket rate limit on the Brightfield route at the APAC edge to blunt the retry storm (will surface client 429s intentionally but reduce backend queueing).
2) Temporarily increase backend pool capacity (scale up dedicated workers in ap-southeast-2).
3) If needed, failover a portion (~30%) of Brightfield traffic to our EU pool to reduce load on APAC NLBs — requires commercial signoff (cost).

ETA: rate limit + scale up in ~12–18 minutes. I'll post follow-ups with metrics.

Attachment: debug_snapshot_0608.tar.gz (logs + traces)

-Hiro
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: URGENT: APAC production errors — elevated 502/504 and 429s

Adding notes from runtime ops and risk:
- No recent deployment touches to generation model code in APAC in the last 24h. This looks capacity + client-behavior (retry) related.
- If we do cross-region overflow, we should:
  * Announce a soft degraded mode to Brightfield (latency increase but reduced error rate).
  * Apply a traffic-split policy with 10% -> 30% to EU, monitor 5 min buckets.
  * Enable aggressive KV-prefix caching for Brightfield routes to reduce token compute for repeated requests.

Cost/implication: temporary cross-region overflow will increase egress and compute burn; asking for quick approval from ops leadership for the overspend.

Grace O'Connor
Lead SRE, Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 02:20:00 +0000
Subject: Exec decision needed: short-term cross-region overflow for Brightfield (APAC)

Tessa — we need your approval to proceed with the temporary cross-region overflow to EU and to accept the overspend for the duration of the incident. Summary of recommended plan:

- Apply APAC edge rate-limits (50 rps token bucket) for the impacted Brightfield routes immediately (SRE will do this).
- Scale up ap-southeast-2 backend pool by +40% (runtime ops).
- Execute traffic split: 25% of Brightfield traffic -> EU pool; monitor error-rate & latencies.
- Communicate to Brightfield that this is a temporary degraded-latency mode; provide a timeline for rollback once stable.

Rationale: Without overflow, we will continue to see client retries and backend queueing that keeps 504/502 elevated. Overflow is the fastest path to reduce immediate user-facing errors.

Estimated cost impact (rough): additional compute + egress ~USD 3–6k per hour until stable. We expect error rate to drop within 10–15 minutes after split.

Please respond with GO / NO-GO. If NO-GO, we will alternate back to pure rate-limiting and wait for backend scaling (slower).

— Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Runtime ops: pool scaled by +40% at 02:57 UTC.

Current metrics (03:20 UTC): 502/504 rate down 65% vs peak; 429s still present but decreasing. Clients report reduced timeouts.

Next steps:
- Run a 4-hour observation window, then roll back traffic split incrementally if stable.
- Postmortem to include: client retry patterns, whether additional per-client backoff guidance is required, and any changes to default retry headers.

Tessa Morgan
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

- 429s decreased by ~55% after rate-limits and customer-side throttling guidance.
- No model or runtime code rollback required.

- Account team (Vanessa) to coordinate a customer-facing incident summary and credits if Brightfield requests.
